messages:
jess_support: FYI customer acme-retail opened a SEV about two things: 1) intermittent 504s on the SCIM deprovision endpoint (/v1/scim/Users/bulk) and 2) users still showing as billable for ~12h after deprovision. Customer provided request_ids and some logs.
omar_security: :eyes: can you paste the request_ids + any error snippets? also which org id?
jess_support: Org: acme-retail (org_394). Request IDs: rq_11a2b3, rq_11a2b8, rq_11a2c0. Customer says the 504s line up with KMS errors in their local logs. They attached this snippet: 
```
2025-02-08T22:13:01Z ERROR deprov-processor: failed to decrypt key for tenant org_394: KMSAccessDenied: access denied
at rsrc/kms/client.go:214
context: user=svc-scim, request_id=rq_11a2b3
```
li_devops: Hmm KMSAccessDenied from the deprov worker? That would cause retries and potentially timeouts. Which KMS principal is the service using?
sophie_engineering: The deprovision pipeline uses the tenant-specific wrapped key flow. If the unwrap call fails the job hits our retry/backoff loop — we do up to 5 attempts, then surface 504 to the API gateway if backend doesn't return.
omar_security: Audit question: customer also says admin audit logs (who/when deleted SCIM users) are missing for the timeframe. audit-bot, can you confirm if any audit entries were generated for org_394 around 2025-02-08 22:00-23:00?
audit-bot: No matching audit entries found for org_394 user deletions between 2025-02-08T21:50:00Z and 2025-02-08T23:00:00Z. (query: audit.event_type:scim.delete AND resource.org_id:org_394)
omar_security: OK that's concerning — deprov retries + missing audit = potential double-failure: KMS denied unwrap and audit pipeline failed to ingest event. We need to check two things in parallel: KMS principal perms and audit pipeline consumer lags.
kevin_billing: On the billing side, customer claims they see tokens/usage charged after the user deletion. We pulled billing events: there are usage entries attributed to user_id: u_7709 for 11:20Z and 11:40Z after the reported deprovevent at 11:05Z. Do we know if the SCIM deprovision completed on our side?
sophie_engineering: If the back-end returned 504 to the client, we may have left the deprov job in limbo. Our deprovision flows are eventually-consistent: delete from SCIM object store -> revoke session tokens -> decrement billing mapping. If unwrap failed mid-process we could have skipped token revocation.
li_devops: I pulled the deprov worker logs. For rq_11a2b3: 
```
worker_deprov: start job user_batch=u:[u_7709,u_7710] req=rq_11a2b3
kms.unwrap: AccessDenied for key=tenant-org_394-key
worker_deprov: retry #1
worker_deprov: retry #2
worker_deprov: timeout 00:01:30 -> job aborted with 504
```
omar_security: Who has permission to call KMS:Decrypt for tenant-org_394-key? iam: `svc-scim@redwood` should, but maybe a rotation/role change removed it. li_devops can you run `gcloud iam get-iam-policy` or equivalent for the key and paste principal list?
li_devops: Running now. Quick results: principal `svc-scim@redwood` is present but the binding is missing `roles/cloudkms.cryptoKeyEncrypterDecrypter` for that key — last update 2025-02-07 03:14Z by infra:role-rotation-bot.
omar_security: That would explain KMSAccessDenied. Need to confirm whether the role-rotation bot change was intentional. @sophie_engineering any scheduled infra key rotation for org_394?
sophie_engineering: We scheduled bulk role cleanup on 2025-02-07 to remove unused principals. Looks like svc-scim was flagged as unused in telemetry and removed. That was a mistake. We need to add it back, then re-run deprov jobs for affected request IDs.
kevin_billing: For billing remediation we can create a credit for the affected user-hours between deprov time and when token revocation completed. How many org users impacted? Customer reports ~120 users in the batch but only a handful of deprovs hit 504; billing shows 3 users with post-deprov usage.
omar_security: Action plan: 1) li_devops re-add KMS role for svc-scim on tenant-org_394-key ASAP (P0). 2) li_devops trigger retry of the three failed deprov jobs (rq_11a2b3, rq_11a2b8, rq_11a2c0) — ensure idempotency. 3) audit team to investigate why audit pipeline didn't record deletions and backfill if possible. 4) billing to prepare provisional credits for the 3 users; final after backfill. 5) product/security to propose an RBAC change to prevent role-rotation bot from removing service principals that are still active.
li_devops: Re-adding role now. Command run: 
```
gcloud kms keys add-iam-policy-binding tenant-org_394-key \ 
  --member=serviceAccount:svc-scim@redwood.iam.gserviceaccount.com \ 
  --role=roles/cloudkms.cryptoKeyEncrypterDecrypter
```
li_devops: Role binding added at 2025-02-08T22:45:12Z. Triggering worker retry for rq_11a2b3.
sophie_engineering: Confirmed worker retried and completed for rq_11a2b3: deprov status=success, tokens revoked, audit event queued.
audit-bot: New audit entries detected for org_394: scim.delete events for user_ids [u_7709,u_7710] at 2025-02-08T22:47:30Z (source=deprov-worker-3).\e kevin_billing: Based on logs, u_7709 had two usage lines after initial deprov attempt; we can credit those and any meter ticks until 22:47:30Z. I'll prepare a provisional $XX credit and loop in account team.
omar_security: Two follow-ups: - Sophie, please add an allowlist filter to the role-rotation job to ignore principals tagged `svc-*` for now. - Audit team, add a monitoring alert if scim.delete events are missing for >5min after a deprov success.
sophie_engineering: Will do. Also adding a safety: if KMS unwrap retries fail, mark job as "failed-with-retry-required" (so we don't return 504 without explicit retry ticket).\ess: thanks everyone. I'll send acme-retail a consolidated note: root cause = accidental role removal by role-rotation; impact = some deprovs retried and completed later leading to short post-deprov billing; remediation = role restored, jobs retried, audit backfilled, provisional credits issued. ETA for formal postmortem and RBAC hardening: 48 hours. :thumbsup:
